chunks: Safwan, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): A man comes to me with silver (dirhams) to sell to me, wanting by it the silver that I have. It is certain that he does not want the dinars, he wants only the silver, and he does not rise until he takes my silver. So I buy the dirhams for him with the dinars, and his dinars are not with me complete, so I borrow from him from my neighbor, and I give it to him to complete his dinars, and perhaps I do not secure its weight. He said: Does he not take the full amount of what is for him? I said: Yes. He said: There is no problem with it.

key_terms.لَيْسَ بِهِ بَأْسٌ: There is no problem with it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to buy silver with gold by borrowing the gold dinars to complete the payment?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of *sarf* (currency exchange) when the buyer lacks immediate possession (*qabd*) of the full gold amount, relying instead on borrowing to complete the payment. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the transaction provided the seller receives the full agreed value (*wafa'*), highlighting the Shia scholarly emphasis on the completion of the exchange rather than strict simultaneous possession of the exact physical coins at the moment of contract. This ruling facilitates commercial liquidity while maintaining the integrity of the exchange contract.

en.hubeali: Safwan, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The man came to me with the silver (Dirhams) to sell to me wanting by it the silver (Dirhams) which I had on me. So it is certain that he did not want the Dinars, not wanting except for the silver (Dirhams), and he did not arise (to leave) until he took my silver (Dirhams). So I bought the Dirhams for him with the Dinars, and his dinars were not with me completely, and I borrowed from him from my neighbour, and I gave it to him to complete his Dinars and maybe I did not achieve its weight’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Is it not that he took the total of that which was for him?’ I said, ‘Yes’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it’.
en.sarwar: 17. Safwan has narrated from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

about the case of a man who came to me with dirham to sell them to me for the dirhams with me. He certainly did not want dinars but he wanted the dirham and he did not leave until he took my dirham. I bought from him dirham in exchange for dinars. His dinars were not with me in complete form so I borrowed from my neighbor and gave to him and perhaps I did not pay attention how much it weighed. He (the Imam) said, Ts it not the case that he takes it to offset what belongs to him?’ I replied, ‘Yes, that is true. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful/”
